tour.overview:
On the border between Brazil and Argentina, the Iguazu river falls over a horseshoe of basalt cliffs almost 3 kilometres long in some 275 separate waterfalls. At its heart, the Devil's Throat sends about half the river down an 80-metre chasm in a permanent cloud of spray. The falls and the subtropical forest around them are protected by two national parks, both UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

This private two-day tour shows both sides with a licensed guide and a car: the Brazilian side, with the best panorama, a boat ride beneath the falls and the bird park, and the Argentine side, where walkways lead right over the water to the edge of the Devil's Throat. One night in Foz do Iguaçu is included.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: 2 days, 1 night
• Start: Foz do Iguaçu airport or your hotel
• End: Foz do Iguaçu airport or your hotel
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver; 1 night with breakfast
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability, your hotel and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy to moderate; several kilometres of walkways

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Brazilian side of the falls.
• The Macuco boat safari.
• The Parque das Aves.
• The Argentine side: the Upper and Lower Circuits.
• The Devil’s Throat.

WHY THIS WORKS
The two sides are complementary: Brazil gives the panorama, Argentina takes you into the falls. With a private car and guide, the border crossing is quick and the days run at your pace.

WHO IT SUITS
Nature lovers, families, couples and photographers.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you only have one day, ask us for the Brazilian side with the boat ride; we can also add the Itaipu dam.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
You need your passport for the Argentine side; check the entry rules for your nationality. The boat ride is wet: bring a change of clothes or a waterproof bag. The falls are fullest from December to March.

days.name: The Brazilian side, the Macuco boat ride and the Parque das Aves
days.description:
What to expect: the great panorama of the falls and a boat ride beneath them.

Your guide and driver meet you at Foz do Iguaçu airport or your hotel at about 9:00. You start at the Parque das Aves, a bird sanctuary in the forest by the park entrance, where you walk through large aviaries among toucans, scarlet macaws and flamingos, many of them rescued from trafficking.

In the national park, you take the Macuco Safari: an open vehicle through the forest, a short walk, and then a fast boat up the river through the rapids and into the spray at the foot of the falls, a thrilling soaking. After lunch (not included), you walk the 1.2-kilometre trail along the Brazilian bank, with the whole sweep of the falls across the gorge, ending on a walkway that juts over the river towards the Devil's Throat, with rainbows in the spray on sunny afternoons. A lift takes you up to the viewpoint, and your driver takes you to your hotel.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
09:00 – Pick-up at the airport or your hotel.
09:30 – Parque das Aves.
11:30 – Macuco Safari boat ride.
13:30 – Lunch break.
14:30 – Brazilian side trail and walkway.
17:00 – Check in at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Bring a swimsuit or quick-dry clothes and a waterproof bag for the boat.
• Do not feed the coatis; they bite.
• A helicopter flight over the falls can be added.

INCLUDED: transfers, guide, park entrance, boat safari, bird park.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, dinner, helicopter.

Overnight: 4-star hotel in Foz do Iguaçu.
Meals: none.

days.name: The Argentine side and the Devil’s Throat
days.description:
What to expect: walkways over the falls and the edge of the Devil’s Throat.

After breakfast you cross the border into Argentina with your guide, about 30 minutes to the Iguazú National Park. A small jungle train takes you to the start of a walkway of more than a kilometre over the wide upper river, to a platform on the very lip of the Devil's Throat, where the water thunders down into the mist.

You return by train and walk the Upper Circuit, along the top of the falls, and the Lower Circuit, a forest trail with views up to the cascades and San Martín island. Lunch is at a restaurant in the park. Toucans, capuchin monkeys and huge blue morpho butterflies are often seen. You cross back into Brazil and are driven to the airport or your hotel.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:00 – Breakfast and border crossing.
09:00 – Jungle train to the Devil’s Throat.
11:00 – Upper Circuit.
12:30 – Lunch in the park.
13:30 – Lower Circuit.
15:30 – Drive back to Brazil.
16:30 – Airport or hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Bring your passport.
• Book an evening flight, from 18:30 onwards.
• On full-moon nights, the Argentine park offers moonlight walks to the Devil’s Throat.

INCLUDED: transfers, guide, park entrance, train, lunch.
NOT INCLUDED: dinner, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: breakfast, lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability, hotels and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Do we need a passport?
faq.answer: Yes, for the Argentine side. Check whether you need a visa for Argentina.

faq.question: Which side is better?
faq.answer: Both: Brazil gives the panorama, Argentina takes you close to the falls. We recommend seeing both.

faq.question: Will we get wet?
faq.answer: On the boat ride, completely; on the walkways near the Devil’s Throat, a little.

faq.question: Is the boat ride safe?
faq.answer: Yes. It is run by a licensed operator with life jackets. It is not recommended for pregnant women or people with back problems.

faq.question: When are the falls fullest?
faq.answer: From December to March, in the rainy season; in dry years they can be lower in August and September.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the boat, the coatis and the train. The boat ride has a minimum age of about 2 years.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. Most walkways are flat; the Brazilian side has a lift and the Devil’s Throat walkway is level.

faq.question: Can we add the Itaipu dam?
faq.answer: Yes, one of the largest hydroelectric dams in the world, on an extra half day.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Light, quick-dry clothes, a rain jacket, sandals or shoes that can get wet, sun protection and insect repellent.

faq.question: What kind of hotel is used?
faq.answer: A comfortable 4-star hotel in Foz do Iguaçu; a hotel inside the national park can be booked on request.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Brazil but never required. If you were happy with your guide and driver, a small tip at the end of the day is a kind gesture.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 72 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
